**Relation to read:** `usp_cl.legislator_terms`

This relation holds historical legislator terms, so you query it by `congress_start`/`congress_end` (or term start/end dates) to find who held a seat during the 117th Congress (2021–2022). It is the correct source because it records terms as time-bounded intervals, letting you filter to a specific past Congress and a specific past date within it. To name the person, join to `usp_cl.legislators` on `bioguide_id` (the reliable, referentially-intact path) and select `official_full` — `legislator_terms` itself has no name column.

**Why the present-day-only view is inadequate:** `usp_cl.mv_current_lawmakers` is a materialized view that returns only the currently sitting member(s). It has no historical timeline, so it cannot tell you who held the seat as of a past date or during the 117th Congress specifically — a member may have left, been replaced, or lost re-election since. Using it for a historical question would return the wrong (current) officeholder or none at all. The playbook's anti-pattern is explicit on this: current-only views cannot answer historical or timeline questions.
